elements.element: Customer owns all Deliverables created for it.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2 instead provides that Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer.

elements.element: Customer owns all work product created for it.
elements.evidence: No Customer ownership of work product is stated; the only relevant ownership language gives Vendor exclusive ownership of every Deliverable.

elements.element: Vendor assigns ownership of the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: There is no assignment to Customer, and Section 14.2 expressly preserves Vendor ownership.

elements.element: Vendor retains ownership of its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3 states that Vendor retains Vendor Technology, while Section 14.1 preserves Customer's independently developed intellectual property.

elements.element: Vendor grants Customer a licence to all Vendor intellectual property embedded in or required to use the Deliverables.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3 provides that, to the extent Vendor Technology is incorporated in or required to use a Deliverable, the licence in Section 13.2 applies.

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor intellectual property is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3 expressly characterizes the incorporated-Vendor-Technology licence as perpetual.

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor intellectual property is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3 does not state that this licence is irrevocable, and the referenced Section 13.2 language was not supplied.

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor intellectual property is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3 does not state that this licence is royalty-free, and the referenced Section 13.2 language was not supplied.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: Section 14.1 states that Customer owns all Customer Data and grants Vendor only a limited processing right.

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own the Deliverables, Customer Data, or relevant intellectual property.
elements.evidence: The clause uses exclusive and party-specific ownership allocations: Vendor exclusively owns Deliverables, while Customer owns Customer Data and its independently developed intellectual property.

elements.element: Vendor owns its generic tools.
elements.evidence: Vendor retains Vendor Technology under Section 14.3 and, more broadly, exclusively owns every Deliverable under Section 14.2, preserving its ownership of generic tools.

elements.element: Vendor owns its know-how.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3 preserves Vendor Technology, and no provision assigns Vendor know-how to Customer.

elements.element: Customer receives a licence to all Deliverables.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2 grants Customer a licence to each Deliverable.

elements.element: The Deliverables licence is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2 expressly states that the licence is perpetual.

elements.element: The Deliverables licence is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2 expressly states that the licence is irrevocable.

elements.element: The Deliverables licence is worldwide.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2 expressly states that the licence is worldwide.

elements.element: The Deliverables licence is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2 expressly states that the licence is royalty-free.

elements.element: The Deliverables licence permits Customer to use the Deliverables.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2 expressly permits Customer to use each Deliverable.

elements.element: The Deliverables licence permits Customer to modify the Deliverables.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2 expressly permits Customer to modify each Deliverable.

elements.element: The Deliverables licence permits Customer to sublicense the Deliverables.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2 expressly permits Customer to sublicense each Deliverable.

elements.element: The Deliverables licence covers Customer's business purposes.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2 grants the specified rights 'for its business.'

result.reason: The operative language does not reach the preferred position because Vendor retains exclusive ownership of Deliverables and makes no assignment to Customer. The incorporated-Vendor-Technology licence is expressly perpetual but is not shown to be irrevocable or royalty-free. The rendered clause does, however, reach the fallback: Vendor's tools, technology, and know-how remain with Vendor, while Customer receives the required perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free rights to use, modify, and sublicense every Deliverable for its business. The change is confined to the Deliverables licence and leaves the Customer Data and Vendor Technology allocations intact without contradiction.
